title: 環境・エネルギー機械
subtitle: Energy and Advanced Fluid Mechanics
educationalGoal: This course deals with energy related to mechanical engineering from various angles. First, students will learn about the environment and energy issues that are becoming widespread problems in modern society. Among the various energy machines in the mechanical field, especially in the fluid-related field, students will learn the basics of the mechanism, performance, and design of fluid machines such as pumps and turbines. In addition, students will learn how to examine environmental issues from the viewpoint of fluid dynamics and/or GX using CFD.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain energy problems in Japan.
Be able to explain energy conversion using turbomachinery.
Be able to understand the principles of pumps, wind turbines and turbines and perform performance calculations.
Be able to use CFD for basic flow condition
Be able to actively discuss issues and outcomes about issues in the local community.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) To be able to explain recent and expected energy problems and directions for solving them.
(2) To be able to explain the energy conversion using turbomachinery in detail with specific examples.
(3) Understand the principles of pumps, wind turbines, and turbines, and be able to calculate their performance.
(4) To be able to carry out flow analysis using CFD and discuss the results.
(5) To be able to examine various environmental problems from the viewpoint of fluid mechanics, and to be able to present and discuss the contents effectively.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1)To be able to explain the expected energy problems.
(2) Explain energy conversion using turbomachinery.
(3) To be able to explain the principles of pumps, wind turbines and turbines.
(4) To be able to perform simple flow analysis using CFD
(5) To be able to examine various environmental problems and present the results

Students are required to conduct a CFD study
 on the important topics of this course
(especially issues including contributions
to the local community) and submit a report.

Students will make presentations on the
contents of the reports using PowerPoint
and posters, and discuss them.
